prompt.es: Escribe una nota a un amigo con tres modismos y una versión sencilla (60-140 palabras).

answer.text: Hi Sam! I'm a bit under the weather today, but we're in the same boat: the exam is tomorrow and we are not ready. I will bite the bullet and hit the books tonight, so please don't overdo the jokes when we study together! In plain English: I feel slightly ill, we have the same exam, and I must study a lot tonight. I will work hard, so please be serious and help me to pass. We can do it together if we stay calm.

es: Contar una anécdota de un día caótico con modismos bien integrados y explicar dos de ellos a alguien que no los conoce.

vocabulary.es: es decir, dicho de otra manera

teaching.en: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday.
teaching.es: Te voy a contar una anécdota de mi caótico lunes.
teaching.explanationEs: Anecdote = anécdota; esta fórmula abre la historia y avisa al oyente de lo que viene.
segments: Let me tell you an
anecdote about my chaotic Monday.
teaching.audioText: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday.

teaching.en: My morning was chaotic: first my bus broke down, and then my phone died. That was the last straw.
teaching.es: Mi mañana fue caótica: primero se averió mi autobús y luego se quedó sin batería mi teléfono. Fue la gota que colmó el vaso.
teaching.explanationEs: The last straw = lo último que hace que ya no puedas más.
segments: My morning was chaotic: first my bus broke down, and
then my phone died. That was the last straw.
teaching.audioText: My morning was chaotic: first my bus broke down, and then my phone died. That was the last straw.

teaching.en: Luckily, the meeting was cancelled, so the bad morning was a blessing in disguise.
teaching.es: Por suerte, la reunión se canceló, así que la mala mañana fue un mal que vino bien.
teaching.explanationEs: A blessing in disguise = algo malo que resulta ser bueno.
segments: Luckily, the meeting was cancelled, so the
bad morning was a blessing in disguise.
teaching.audioText: Luckily, the meeting was cancelled, so the bad morning was a blessing in disguise.

teaching.en: We ran to the station and, luckily, we arrived in the nick of time.
teaching.es: Corrimos a la estación y, por suerte, llegamos justo a tiempo.
teaching.explanationEs: In the nick of time = en el último momento, justo antes de que fuera tarde.
segments: We ran to the station and, luckily,
we arrived in the nick of time.
teaching.audioText: We ran to the station and, luckily, we arrived in the nick of time.

teaching.en: In my anecdote, Dad hit the roof, which means he was very angry.
teaching.es: En mi anécdota, papá se puso furioso, lo que significa que estaba muy enfadado.
teaching.explanationEs: Which means + explicación sencilla aclara un modismo a quien no lo conoce.

which means he was very angry.

teaching.explanationEs: In other words reformula el modismo con palabras sencillas.

prompt.es: Cuenta tu lunes caótico con cuatro modismos y explica dos (70-150 palabras).

answer.text: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday. First, I was under the weather, which means I felt a bit ill, but I went to work anyway. Then my bus broke down, and my phone died: that was the last straw, in other words, I could not take any more. I ran to the office and arrived in the nick of time, and my boss did not hit the roof. Luckily, the meeting was cancelled, so my bad day was a blessing in disguise. By and large, it was a difficult day, but it is a funny anecdote now.
accepted: Let me tell you an anecdote about my chaotic Monday. First, I was under the weather, which means I felt a bit ill, but I went to work anyway. Then my bus broke down, and my phone died: that was the last straw, in other words, I could not take any more. I ran to the office and arrived in the nick of time, and my boss did not hit the roof. Luckily, the meeting was cancelled, so my bad day was a blessing in disguise. By and large, it was a difficult day, but it is a funny anecdote now.

Yesterday was a chaotic day, and I want to tell you an anecdote. In the morning I was on cloud nine because I got good news, but then my phone died, and my bus broke down. That was the last straw, which means I could not take any more. Luckily, a friend drove me, and I reached the class in the nick of time. The exam was a piece of cake, so the bad morning turned out to be a blessing in disguise, in other words, a bad start with a happy ending.

feedback.es: La anécdota sigue una secuencia, integra cuatro modismos y explica al menos dos con which means o in other words.

origin.text: Escribe una anécdota de un día caótico. Usa cuatro modismos de las clases anteriores y explica dos de ellos con which means o in other words, como para alguien que no los conoce.
